job.style: a passage that starts from a common wrong idea and corrects it

passage: Many students believe that rusting is simply a layer of dirt or mud that accumulates on iron objects over time. However, rusting is actually a chemical change where iron reacts with oxygen and moisture to form a new substance called iron oxide. Unlike a physical change where the material remains the same, this process permanently alters the chemical composition of the metal. While some people think only iron can corrode, many other metals also react with their environment, though they may form different protective layers. Furthermore, there is a common misconception that all metals are extremely hard solids that cannot be cut. In reality, elements like sodium and potassium are soft enough to be sliced easily with a knife. Another frequent error is assuming that all non-metals are poor conductors of electricity. While most non-metals are insulators, graphite, a form of carbon, is an excellent conductor. Finally, when metals react with acids, they do not simply vanish or turn into liquid; they undergo a chemical reaction to form new compounds and often release hydrogen gas. Understanding these properties helps us distinguish between physical changes and chemical reactions in the world around us.

items.evidence: However, rusting is actually a chemical change where iron reacts with oxygen and moisture to form a new substance called iron oxide.
items.q: An iron gate turns reddish-brown after the rainy season. What has happened to its surface?
options: Its iron has formed a new substance
Mud and dirt have stuck onto the iron
Only its colour changed; it is still iron
Rain water has melted some of the iron
items.explain: Iron reacted with oxygen and moisture, forming a new substance, iron oxide. This is rust.

wrong.why: thinks rust is a layer of dirt or mud
thinks rusting is only a colour change
thinks the metal turns into liquid

items.evidence: In reality, elements like sodium and potassium are soft enough to be sliced easily with a knife.
items.q: Meena slices a piece of sodium with a kitchen knife. What does this show?
options: Some metals are soft enough to cut easily
Sodium is a non-metal, since metals are hard
All metals can be cut with a sharp knife
Sodium has rusted and become soft like mud
items.explain: Sodium is a metal, yet it is soft enough to slice. So not all metals are hard.

wrong.why: thinks all metals are hard, so sodium cannot be one
turns one example into a rule for all metals
thinks rust is soft mud on the metal

items.evidence: While most non-metals are insulators, graphite, a form of carbon, is an excellent conductor.
items.q: Priya puts a graphite rod into a circuit with a bulb. What will happen?
options: The bulb glows, as graphite conducts well
The bulb stays off, as non-metals never conduct
The bulb glows, as graphite is a metal
The bulb stays off, as carbon is an insulator
items.explain: Graphite is a form of carbon, a non-metal, but it conducts electricity very well.

wrong.why: thinks only metals can conduct, so graphite must be one
applies 'most non-metals are insulators' to all of them

items.evidence: Finally, when metals react with acids, they do not simply vanish or turn into liquid; they undergo a chemical reaction to form new compounds and often release hydrogen gas.
items.q: A zinc piece disappears in dilute acid while bubbles form. What happened to the zinc?
options: It changed into new compounds, giving off gas
It was destroyed and no longer exists
It melted and simply turned into liquid
It dissolved without any chemical change
items.explain: The zinc reacted with the acid to form new compounds and released hydrogen gas as bubbles.

wrong.why: thinks a metal that disappears has been destroyed
thinks the metal just turned into liquid
thinks the change is only physical
